sub_graphs.title: Altair Light Client: Stuck Sync Recovery
sub_graphs.description: Models the error recovery mechanism when the light client sync process stalls

nodes.label: Light Client Tracking Chain
nodes.description: Light client is in normal real-time tracking mode

nodes.label: Detect Sync Stall
nodes.description: Detect that no finality updates have been received for an extended period

nodes.label: Light Client Sync Stalled
nodes.description: Light client has not received finality updates and sync appears stuck

nodes.label: Apply Forced Update
nodes.description: Force-apply the best available pending update to advance the light client state

nodes.label: Light Client Recovered
nodes.description: Light client state advanced via forced update, can resume normal tracking

ambiguities.text: The specification states the trusted block root should be 'within the weak subjectivity period' but does not define the exact duration or how to compute it for this context.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the weak subjectivity period follows the standard Ethereum definition based on validator set size and churn, typically around 2 weeks for mainnet. Implementations should use the compute_weak_subjectivity_period function.

ambiguities.text: The specification does not detail what 'sync appears stuck' means precisely, or the exact timeout before forced updates are applied.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume the sync protocol specification defines the specific timeout and conditions for force updates. The light client should apply a forced update if no finality update has been processed for an entire sync committee period.

implicit_assumptions.description: The trusted block root provided out-of-band is assumed to correspond to a genuinely finalized block on the canonical chain.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the trusted root points to a non-canonical or forged block, the light client will follow a fake chain, accepting attacker-controlled state as valid.

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot control more than 2/3 of the sync committee to forge finality updates.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: A supermajority-controlled sync committee could produce valid-looking updates for arbitrary blocks, completely deceiving the light client.

implicit_assumptions.description: The light client can access at least one honest full node to fetch bootstrap data and updates.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If all data sources are malicious, the light client could be eclipsed and fed stale or incorrect data, potentially missing important chain events.
